offer.title: Offer information
offer.intro: At this stage SkateLab does not take payment on the site, enter agreements through a web form or provide public web-app access. This page is not a public offer.
offer.p1: The site introduces a mobile app for iPhone, iPad and Android and lets visitors request a pilot conversation. Pilot scope, equipment, timing, price and handling of materials will be agreed separately before work begins.
offer.p2: Project enquiries: https://t.me/xpos587. Do not send video, sensor data, health information or children’s data in your first message. The operator and legal enquiry process still require confirmation.
offer.p3: If a paid pilot or other service is offered, its scope, price, payment, acceptance, cancellation and refund terms will be set out in a separate document naming the operator and its details. No such document is published now.
offer.p4: The process for legal enquiries is described in the draft notice at the top of this page.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These terms describe use of the public SkateLab website and requests for information about a pilot. Public web-app access, account creation and material uploads are not currently offered through this site.
terms.p1: SkateLab is an informational site about a mobile app in development for iPhone, iPad and Android devices. Feature descriptions are informational and do not promise availability, compatibility or a particular result.
terms.p2: Project enquiries: https://t.me/xpos587. Do not send video, sensor data, health information or children’s data in your first message. The operator and legal enquiry process still require confirmation.
terms.p3: The SkateLab name, copy, design, code and site materials belong to their rights holders or are used lawfully. Use beyond personal review requires permission or a legal exception.
terms.p4: The site is provided as it is. We do not guarantee uninterrupted operation, availability in a particular country, suitability for a sports or medical purpose, or a sports outcome. The site does not replace a coach, doctor or other qualified professional.
terms.p5: Terms may change with the site and product. Governing law and other mandatory details will follow the confirmed owner information described in the notice at the top of this page.
terms.p6: The process for legal enquiries is described in the draft notice at the top of this page and will be clarified before publication.

landing.heroKicker: A tool for figure skating schools
landing.heroTitle: Every attempt Clearer to the coach
landing.heroLead: Video and movement data give coach and skater a shared language. Keep the context of an attempt and find a question for the next practice.
landing.heroAlt: Adult figure skater gliding on the ice during practice
landing.stage: From a complete recording to one clear action
landing.storyTitle: From capture to the next attempt
landing.storyIntro: The coach captures the right moment, connects its context and defines the next step for the skater in a mobile app.
landing.bladeAlt: Close-up of a figure skate blade on the ice
landing.storyCaptureBody: A phone or camera records the attempt where the coach needs to return to a detail. Recording conditions are agreed for the chosen task.
landing.storySenseBody: Video and sensor data are designed as shared context: not a replacement for observation, but a way to check it more precisely.
landing.storyReviewBody: The coach sees the attempt, method limits and a question for the next practice. Automated output is not a score for the skater.
landing.reviewTitle: The decision stays with the coach
landing.reviewLead: It shortens the path from “I think” to a question that can be checked in the next practice.
landing.coachImageAlt: Coach and adult skater reviewing footage together on a tablet
landing.reviewOneBody: Connect the recording to one element and moment.
landing.reviewTwoBody: Keep video, data and method limits together.
landing.reviewThreeBody: Leave the skater with a decision and a testable task.
landing.questionsTitle: Start with the task Then the hardware
landing.answer1: The current product has an uploaded-video analysis flow. The exact element list and limits are agreed before a school pilot.
landing.answer2: Sensors are part of SkateLab’s direction. Video and hardware data need to be checked together for a specific task; we do not promise a universal setup.
landing.answer3: The school and pilot team agree on camera angle, access, storage and permissions in advance. Recordings of minors require separate consent.
landing.pilotTitle: Let’s test one real task from your school
landing.pilotBody: Tell us which element or coach workflow you want to examine. We will define the pilot, equipment and evaluation criteria before the first practice.
landing.pilotNote: Start with the task. No personal videos or children’s data.
landing.footerTagline: Precise feedback for figure skating schools

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This version applies to the public SkateLab marketing site. The site currently has no public registration, account sign-in, video upload or lead form. The app and pilot are in development.
privacy.p1: The operator, country, contact email and governing jurisdiction are identified in the draft notice at the top of this page and have not yet been confirmed by the project owner.
privacy.p2: Project enquiries: https://t.me/xpos587. Do not send video, sensor data, health information or children’s data in your first message. The operator and legal enquiry process still require confirmation.
privacy.p3: Technical delivery and site security; saving your cookie choices; with separate consent, measuring visits and site interactions; and responding if you contact the project team yourself.
privacy.p4: Legal bases, retention periods, international transfers and people with access depend on the operator’s country and actual infrastructure configuration. Their description must match confirmed facts and current data collection.
privacy.p5: Consent choices are stored locally in your browser. Optional analytics and session recordings should start only after consent. Their providers, data categories, retention and transfer settings must be confirmed for the actual deployment; see the Cookie Policy.
privacy.p6: Project enquiries: https://t.me/xpos587. Do not send video, sensor data, health information or children’s data in your first message. The operator and legal enquiry process still require confirmation.
privacy.p7: This policy will be updated when the site, mobile app, analytics or contact process changes. Its date and version must match the document that is actually published.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.intro: The public SkateLab site uses browser local storage and a cookie to remember your choice about optional technologies. Names and lifetimes may depend on deployment configuration.
cookies.p1: The skatelab_consent local-storage key preserves selected consent categories. Saving a choice also writes the skatelab_consent cookie with path=/, max-age=31536000 (one year) and SameSite=Lax. The old consent_accepted setting is used only for migration and is removed after it is read.
cookies.p2: After analytics consent, the app calls PostHog through the proxied /ingest route. PostHog and its library may create their own technical storage; exact names, provider, processing location, event set and retention must match the actual deployment configuration and the draft notice.
cookies.p3: After separate recording consent, the app starts PostHog session recording. Without that choice it calls the recording stop method. Before this feature is used, masking, access and retention must be confirmed consistently with the draft notice.
cookies.p4: You can reject optional categories, change your browser settings or delete the site’s local data. Deleting the settings will show the consent banner again.
cookies.p5: The operator, contact email, country, governing law, providers, retention periods and withdrawal process are identified in the draft notice and require confirmation before the final version is published.

publicSite.blogIntro: Practical notes on recording, data and the conversation between coach and skater. So the next attempt starts with a clear task.
publicSite.recordingAlt: Coach filming an adult figure skater with a phone held horizontally
publicSite.notesAlt: Open notebook, pencil, gloves and a powered-off tablet beside the rink
publicSite.processIntro: More than watching a jump again. Find the moment, check its context and choose one task for the next attempt.
publicSite.captureBody: Record the approach, element and exit in one continuous clip. Keeping the torso, arms and skates in frame gives the coach context, not just a striking still.
publicSite.phaseIntro: A jump is a sequence of connected actions. Select a phase to see what deserves attention. This is a movement diagram, not an instruction for performing the element.
publicSite.phaseCaption: Movement diagram, not a measurement of this recording
publicSite.phaseBody0: Watch the full approach: direction of travel, torso position and arm preparation. One frame cannot explain how the skater arrived at takeoff.
publicSite.phaseBody1: Compare the last ice contact with the beginning of flight. A blurred skate or hidden support limits how precisely that moment can be located.
publicSite.phaseBody2: Follow changes in arm and torso position between frames. A single view cannot reliably recover the full three-dimensional orientation of the body.
publicSite.phaseBody3: Do not stop at first contact. Watch how the skater maintains position and continues the exit after touching the ice.
publicSite.reviewTitle: The frame and the question, side by side
publicSite.reviewIntro: The coach connects an observation to the conditions of the attempt. This sequence separates what the recording shows from what we assume.
publicSite.reviewCaption: Illustration of the review sequence, not an athlete report
publicSite.reviewPrompt2: Which one task goes back on the ice?
publicSite.reviewBody0: Select an attempt and locate the transition from flight to landing. Watch the movement first, then return to individual frames.
publicSite.reviewBody1: Keep the original camera angle, skate visibility and recording quality in view. If the support is hidden, leave the question open instead of replacing it with a precise number.
publicSite.reviewBody2: Agree one action with the coach and a sign you can check in the next recording. Do not change everything at once.
publicSite.reviewNote0: Keep frames before and after contact
publicSite.reviewNote1: Check whether ice contact is visible
publicSite.reviewNote2: Compare the next attempt from the same angle
publicSite.taskTitle: The next attempt starts with the review
publicSite.taskBody: Useful feedback is short: what we noticed, what we are checking and how we will recognise a change. Technique and training load decisions stay with the coach.
publicSite.limitsBody: Video depends on camera angle, light and occlusion. Sensor data depends on calibration and synchronisation. SkateLab does not replace coaching, judging or medical assessment.
publicSite.equipmentIntro: A useful review starts with a clear recording, not an equipment purchase. Extra data earns its place when there is a specific question about movement.
publicSite.equipmentSceneIntro: Video shows the external picture. An inertial sensor describes motion in its own coordinate system. Comparing them requires a shared timeline and checked recording conditions.
publicSite.sourceBody0: A camera preserves body position in the image and the sequence of actions. Scene depth and the hidden side of the body remain uncertain.
publicSite.sourceBody1: An inertial sensor records acceleration and angular velocity. Orientation requires processing and calibration; edge use and glide cannot be read directly from one signal.
publicSite.equipmentCaption: Source diagram, not a device design or mounting method
publicSite.compareV0: Body position in the image, approach and exit
publicSite.compareS0: Acceleration and angular velocity in sensor coordinates
publicSite.compareV1: Angle, body visibility, sharpness and frame rate
publicSite.compareV2: One frame for precise three-dimensional movement
publicSite.compareS2: One signal for a judgement of element quality
publicSite.setup0: Agree recording with the rink and participants. Avoid capturing bystanders unnecessarily.
publicSite.setup1: Choose a safe spot outside skating paths. A tripod must not block access.
publicSite.setup2: Keep the whole skater in frame from approach through the end of the exit.
publicSite.setup3: Keep the original file without messenger compression or interpolated frames.
publicSite.hardwareBody: Do not choose a sensor from a picture. Compatibility, mounting and the test scenario need a separate discussion. This is not a device catalogue, confirmed specification sheet or offer to buy a kit.
publicSite.equipmentAnswer0: No. Discuss the task and recording conditions first. If inertial data is needed, agree the equipment and safe mounting before recording.
publicSite.equipmentAnswer1: Start by checking a recording: the whole skater is visible, skates are distinguishable and motion is not blurred. This page does not provide a universal list of compatible models.
publicSite.equipmentAnswer2: There is no guarantee. Raw data access, timestamps, calibration and export format matter. Send the model and task, not personal recordings in the first message.
publicSite.contactTitle: Start with your task on the ice
publicSite.contactIntro: School, coach or skater — tell us which moment you want to understand. A first conversation needs no footage, sensors or registration.
publicSite.contactDirect: A direct conversation with the project team
publicSite.contactBody: Message on Telegram: who you are, the element or workflow you want to examine and how you record practice today. We will discuss whether and how a joint evaluation could work.
publicSite.contactPrivacy: Do not send children’s recordings, medical information or other personal data in your first message. Access and permissions need a separate discussion.
publicSite.audienceBody0: How review fits a lesson, who sees recordings and what a useful result would mean for your coaches.
publicSite.audienceBody1: Which moment is unclear, what context is missing and how you explain the next task to the skater.
publicSite.audienceBody2: What you want to discuss with the coach. Begin with a movement question, not a personal video.
publicSite.contactQuestion0: Can I download the app now?
publicSite.contactAnswer0: Public mobile app downloads are not open yet. Message us to discuss a use case or interest in future access.
publicSite.contactQuestion1: Am I signing up for a paid programme?
publicSite.contactAnswer1: No. A Telegram message starts a conversation, not a subscription or payment obligation. Any collaboration needs a separate agreement.
publicSite.contactQuestion2: Where can I follow the project?
publicSite.contactAnswer2: Practical articles appear in this site’s journal. Use Telegram for questions. No other social account links are confirmed here.
publicSite.closeTitle: A good beginning starts with one question
publicSite.closeBody: Tell us about your practice. Start with the task, recording conditions and what matters to the coach.
publicSite.homeTrackTitle: Record, review, return to the ice
publicSite.homeTrackIntro: From the whole movement to a specific question. Explore a step-by-step review of one attempt.
publicSite.homeStepBody0: Approach, element and exit in one recording — with the beginning intact.
publicSite.homeStepBody1: Find the phase where a question appears and check the neighbouring frames.
publicSite.homeStepBody2: Leave with one testable task, not a long list of corrections.
publicSite.homeJournalBody: Where to put the camera and how to keep the context — a practical guide for practice.
publicSite.missingTitle: This trace leads off the page
